name: speaker-verification
summary: Local-first speaker verification and target-speaker extraction service for identity-aware audio workflows.
why_it_matters: Speaker verification remains valuable capability knowledge, but it is not part of the current actively validated core resource set and should stay blueprint-level until scenario demand resumes.
when_to_use: A future scenario needs enrolled-speaker verification or separation.
Operators want voice identity checks in local-first audio workflows.
The workflow depends on reusable speaker embeddings or extraction endpoints.

platform_support.notes: The service can run in containers, but model acceleration, audio dependencies, and inference performance vary by environment.

prerequisites: Defined enrollment, storage, and privacy policies
implementation_notes: Promotion should validate a real voice workflow with expected error tolerances.
Keep speaker identity, extraction, and downstream transcription concerns separate.
Privacy and retention behavior must be explicit.
operational_notes: Model runtime requirements and latency matter to operator expectations.
Validation should include known positive and negative verification cases.
Sensitive voice artifacts need clear storage boundaries.
risks: Audio identity workflows are easy to oversell and hard to validate thoroughly.
GPU expectations can silently shape support quality.
